description:
System.halt/0,1 ends the program with a status on interp, run and build, as Elixir's does: any process can halt, a halt can't be caught (no catch, no after), stdout is flushed, halt(n) exits n (the OS keeps the low 8 bits), a negative status raises Elixir's ArgumentError ('errors were found at the given arguments:\n\n  * 1st argument: invalid status\n'), a non-integer raises FunctionClauseError.

Design (page ../fz-sc8.7.html, approved 2026-11-11): a program ends when it halts, and its status is the halt's. ExecCtx gains a halt hook beside spawn/send; each scheduler records Some(status) and its run loop (run_until_idle src/exec/runtime.rs, drive_backend_until_idle src/ir_interp/backend.rs, aot_run_queue_loop runtime/src/aot_shim.rs) stops once a halt is recorded. fz_system_halt flushes the output sink, calls the hook, and marks the caller ended with exit_status = status (the uncaught-raise state without the stderr line), so the existing unwinding runs and no handler search happens. Main ending, normally or by an uncaught raise, records a halt with main's status, so children no longer outlive main (Elixir halts at script end). Each driver reads the recorded status instead of reading main after the loop; RunFailure/CliError map it as now. A run that goes idle without halting keeps today's behavior. OutputSink gains flush(), called at every end: this also fixes a built binary losing a final partial line (IO.write without newline prints nothing today).

The builder first lists every fixture whose output changes when main's end halts; each is brought in line with Elixir or reported before any re-bless.
title: System.halt/1 sets the exit status on all three paths
